request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply:
CBO and JCT projected in their February 2011 baseline that implementing the ACA would reduce federal deficits by $210 billion over FY2012–FY2021 (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). That net estimate factored in projected insurance-coverage expansion costs of $1,390 billion, partly offset by $348 billion, leaving $1,042 billion in net coverage costs over the same period (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7).

These were projections—not a retrospective accounting of what the law ultimately did to the budget. See the [brief](output/briefs/case-20261021-165428-1bc6.html) for details.
reply.reasoning: The verified CRS quote gives the bottom-line deficit projection and supporting coverage cost/offset estimates. Clearly distinguish the February 2011 forecast from realized budget outcomes.
